one_month_reasoning: Inside the window to 2026-11-12: (1) Q3 2026 results, not yet announced; Q2 came on Aug 12 [2], so a date around Nov 10-12 is likely but not certain to fall inside. Guidance is core revenue $214-216M, core GM 38-40% (the trough), core operating margin -23% to -25% [2]. The questions are OpenAI cloud revenue and whether management repeats 'more than triple in 2027'. The stock fell 16% after hours on Q2 [24] and 19.6% on Q1 [35], so a bad print can cost 15-25%. (2) Locked-up supply: staged tranches continued into October (19.4M on Sep 30 [9,23]) and the remaining lock-up ends around mid-November [16]; the supervisor finds this final release is a remainder, not ~171M shares, so I count less supply drag than in round 1. (3) Support: Altman publicly called Cerebras a close partner on Oct 2 [36], short interest is 12.85% of float [14], and the stock sits near its post-IPO low ($145.75). The Ultrafast-on-Nvidia report is unconfirmed and moves no number. Net: median $148 (about flat, slightly below spot) and a 24% one-month log-sd (an assumed ~85% forward vol / 3.5, with the earnings event included).

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: A discount, for structural reasons that last through the horizon. (1) Mix: cloud was 70% of Q2 GAAP revenue and the $25.4B RPO is mostly OpenAI inference capacity [1]; capex was 147% of 6M 2026 revenue [5], so most revenue is capex-heavy cloud revenue that the market prices like CRWV/NBIS. (2) Margins: FY2026 core GM is guided at 41-43% with Q3 the trough at 38-40% [2], below chip peers. (3) Concentration: OpenAI is essentially all of the backlog [17], and the 10-Q lets the $918M loan accelerate if the MRA ends [1]. Mix-weighting gives 7.6-8.0x; ~0.9x more comes off for post-horizon risks.

reverse_dcf_check: At my 14.7% WACC the explicit FY2026-29 cash flows plus a 14x FY2029 EBITDA exit give $86.51, against $136.89 for the 7.0x horizon EV/sales. The engine finds the multiple implies a 5.1% WACC on my cash flows; equivalently, at 14.7% it needs a ~23.8x exit on FY2029 EBITDA of $1.98B (about CoreWeave's 23.5x trailing). With FCF at roughly half of EBITDA, that is a ~2% FCF yield, which at 14.7% requires growth averaging well above 10% a year for a decade after 2029, i.e. the OpenAI capacity renewed and extended plus new customers, and EBIT margins above my 13%. That is plausible only if Cerebras keeps a speed premium against GPU/ASIC inference and OpenAI renews, which the long-dated risks question. So the multiple sits 39% below the peer median and the DCF keeps a 30% weight.

reasoning: Round 2. I accept the supervisor's corrections that I could check at source. (a) Shares: the 10-Q shows Class N rising from 3,682,000 to 13,715,508 by exactly the 10,033,508 vested OpenAI shares, with 23.41M unvested warrant shares and 23.797M options still outstanding. My round-1 count (237.6M +3.5%/yr) left most of that out; I now use 285.66M flat (options gross, since I did not confirm the exercise price). (b) The Ultrafast-on-Nvidia report rests on one unconfirmed social post, and Altman publicly called Cerebras a close partner on Oct 2 [36]. It comes out of every number, so FY2027 returns to the $2.95B consensus. (c) RPO bands: H1-2028 carries the back-loaded rest of band 1. I put FY2028 at $5.4B, a little under the supervisor's ~$5.6B, because capacity is delivered in phases and band 2 is likely back-loaded. (d) CRWV on an EV basis is 4.58x, not 2.2x, so the mix-weighted multiple is 7.6-8.0x. I now take ~0.9x off for post-horizon risks instead of adding +0.5x for own silicon, which gives 7.0x. (e) WACC 14.7%; net cash per F7 with the pledged restricted cash excluded. Skeptic-lane follow-ups: the 424B4 confirms the material weaknesses, and EDGAR full-text search shows the phrase still in both 10-Qs. That is not remediated as far as the filings show (context only, no number). A law firm is soliciting investors over the June 24 drop, but no suit has been filed (negligible value). I found no short-seller report and no October downgrade. The equity-raise risk I missed in round 1 is added; the base path keeps ~$3.6B minimum net cash, so a raise appears only in the bear case. Result: fair value $121.78 (DCF $86.51 x 0.3 + EV/sales $136.89 x 0.7), 18% below spot. Scenarios are $68 / $122 / $191 at 26/51/23%. For the ladder I pull scenario values 20% toward spot (in logs) to allow for my own model error and use a 47% within-scenario log-sd. That gives a median of ~$122 and P(>=$149) = 0.36, a total log-sd of ~0.6 (below the IPO-inflated 115% realized), and a thesis break at $90 (4.3x NTM EV/sales, below CoreWeave). Research this round: 4 searches and ~10 fetches. sec.gov archive pages refused a scripted generic User-Agent, so I read filings with WebFetch and used data.sec.gov XBRL and EDGAR full-text search by script. The forum and crypto-blog sources from round 1 are dropped.
